entry.title: Q3 2026: Quarterly Release Highlights for SAP BAIP Security and Identity & Access Management
entry.content:
Security is constantly evolving - and so are the ways we protect our SAP landscapes. What’s new in SAP BAIP Security and Identity & Access Management? From new capabilities to valuable enhancements, here’s your quarterly roundup of the latest updates you won’t want to miss.

For a complete overview of feature deliveries for SAP Cloud Identity Services, check out our list of all new feature announcements in the SAP Cloud Identity Services Release Notes on the SAP Help Portal.

SAP Cloud Identity Services: Agent identity and IAM for SAP Joule

Agent identity represents AI and automation agents in SAP Cloud Identity Services. Agents can authenticate, receive authorization, and be managed like human users while retaining agent-specific capabilities and security controls. You can find detailed information for administrators on the SAP Help Portal.

We also released the identity and access management architecture required for SAP Joule, including the requirement for a single SAP Cloud Identity Services tenant, SAP-managed provisioning, and global user ID assignment. Understand this foundation before you implement Joule to ensure consistent authentication and authorization across all connected SAP applications.

SAP Cloud Identity Services: SAP-managed SAP Cloud Identity

SAP Cloud Identity Services support both SAP-managed and customer-managed integration models, depending on who is responsible for maintaining and operating the tenant, application and provisioning configurations.

SAP-managed refers to a delivery approach in which SAP is responsible for key technical and operational aspects of the solution. This approach reduces complexity for you and provides a consistent, best-practice experience. SAP manages the software lifecycle, including provisioning, technical integration, monitoring, automatic updates, backups, and offboarding. Customer-managed refers to a delivery approach in which you are responsible for configuring and maintaining your tenants according to your business requirements. This approach allows you to adapt features and functionality to your specific needs.

Identity and access management for SAP BAIP

You can now safely switch an OIDC trust configuration of a BAIP subaccount to another SAP Cloud Identity Services tenant without losing user data, such as authorizations or user-related data in subscribed applications.

For more information, see SAP Note 3468982.

SAP Key Management Service: General availability

SAP Key Management Service (SAP KMS) is now generally available to all SAP customers. It enables the use of customer-managed keys to protect data at rest across SAP cloud products and the SAP Business AI Platform. With consistent key governance and enhanced auditability, SAP KMS helps organizations meet compliance and regulatory requirements while maintaining control over their business data in SAP cloud landscapes.

For more information, please check our product overview and the SAP Help Portal.

SAP Secure Login Service for SAP GUI: Quantum-safe cryptography

We now support quantum-safe cryptography for the communication protocol between SAP GUI and SAP NetWeaver Application Server for ABAP. We have extended the Secure Login Client to integrate quantum-safe cryptography into authentication protocols, and we have enhanced the SAP Cryptographic Library to support quantum-safe authentication for the Secure Network Communications protocol. This helps protect communication channels between SAP GUI desktop clients and SAP NetWeaver Application Server for ABAP. It also prevents quantum computer-based harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks on SAP GUI communications using advanced security measures and ensures long-term communication security by adopting state-of-the-art cryptographic protocols.

For more information on the SAP Secure Login Service for SAP GUI, check the SAP Help Portal.

Join the SAP Business AI Platform Security and SAP Cloud Identity Services communities to get updates, share feedback, and connect with others!

entry.title: How to Delete a Stuck Service Entry Sheet in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud When Originated from SAP BN
entry.content:
Introduction

If you are running SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud integrated with SAP Business Network (formerly Ariba Network) via scope item 42K, you may have run into a frustrating scenario: a supplier submits a Service Entry Sheet (SES) through SAP Business Network, the SES lands in your S/4HANA system — but now, for whatever reason, it needs to be deleted. The PO quantity is blocked, no new SES can be raised against the same PO line, and neither the buyer team in S/4HANA nor the supplier in Business Network can find a way to remove it.

 

This blog post explains exactly why this happens, and gives you two concrete options to resolve it — from a simple configuration setting in Business Network, to a manual SOAP payload workaround for stubborn cases.

 

The Problem Scenario

Let's walk through a typical example that leads to this situation:

 

  1. Supplier creates a Service Entry Sheet in SAP Business Network against a Purchase Order.
  2. The SES syncs to S/4HANA Public Cloud via the managed integration gateway (Communication Arrangement SAP_COM_0237). The SES appears in the Manage Service Entry Sheets Fiori app with status Submitted / In Approval.
  3. The SES has NOT been approved yet — it is sitting in approval or was rejected at the buyer's end.
  4. Supplier realizes the SES was submitted by mistake — wrong quantity, wrong PO line, or created in error.
  5. Supplier looks for a Cancel button in Business Network — it does not exist. There is no cancel option visible to the supplier.
  6. Buyer tries to delete the SES directly in S/4HANA — the system blocks it. Because the SES was created from SAP Business Network, deletion must also originate from Business Network. S/4HANA will not allow a direct manual deletion.
  7. Result: PO line quantity is fully consumed by the stuck SES. No new SES can be created for the same PO line. The procurement process is stuck.

 

Note: This is standard SAP system design — the SES lifecycle is owned by the system that created it. Since SAP Business Network created the SES, the delete instruction must also come from Business Network into S/4HANA via the integration.

 

Root Cause

By default, SAP Business Network does not show a Cancel option to suppliers for Service Entry Sheets they have submitted. The setting that controls this behaviour is disabled out of the box and must be explicitly enabled by the buyer administrator.

 

Additionally, even when the setting is enabled, network delays or integration errors can sometimes cause the cancel request to not flow through to S/4HANA — leaving the SES in an orphaned state on the S/4HANA side.

 

Solution

There are two options available. Start with Option 1 — it is the cleaner, supported approach.

 

Option 1 — Enable 'Allow Suppliers to Cancel Service Sheets' in SAP Business Network   (Recommended)

This is the standard, supported way to resolve the issue. Once enabled, the supplier will see a Cancel button directly in SAP Business Network and can trigger the deletion themselves — the cancel request will flow automatically to S/4HANA via the integration.

 

Steps:

 

  1. Log in to SAP Business Network as the Buyer Administrator.
  2. Go to Company Settings (top-right menu → Company Settings).
  3. Navigate to Service Entry Sheet Settings.
  4. Find the parameter: "Allow suppliers to cancel service sheets that they create"
  5. Enable the setting and save.
  6. Inform the supplier to log back in to SAP Business Network — they will now see a Cancel button on the SES.
  7. Supplier clicks Cancel in Business Network → the delete message is sent automatically to S/4HANA → SES is removed → PO quantity is released.

 

When to use Option 1: Use this whenever possible. It is the clean, system-integrated approach. The cancel flows through the same SOAP interface that originally created the SES, and no manual intervention is needed on the S/4HANA side.

 

Option 2 — Manually Send the Delete Payload via Bruno / Postman

Use this option when:

  • Option 1 is already enabled but the supplier's cancel is stuck and not flowing to S/4HANA.
  • The integration is experiencing errors and the automatic delete message was lost.
  • You need an immediate resolution without waiting for Business Network to process the cancel.

 

This approach simulates what SAP Business Network would send — you manually construct and POST the SOAP delete message directly to the inbound web service in S/4HANA.

 

Step 1 — Get the Service URL from SAP_COM_0237

  1. Log in to SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud.
  2. Open the Communication Arrangements app (search in Fiori Launchpad).
  3. Find the arrangement for scope item 42K: SAP_COM_0237 (Ariba Network — Buyer Integration via SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway).
  4. Under Inbound Services, find: "Service Entry Sheet — Create, Delete (Lean Services)"
  5. Copy the Service URL — it will look like:
    https://<your-s4hana-host>/sap/bc/srt/scs_ext/sap/serviceentrysheetrequest_in

 

Step 2 — Get the Inbound Communication Credentials

  1. In the same Communication Arrangement (SAP_COM_0237), go to the Inbound Communication section.
  2. Copy the Communication User and its password.
  3. Note: This workaround applies when Basic Authentication is configured for the inbound service. If your arrangement uses certificate-based auth, configure your API client accordingly.

 

Step 3 — Construct and Send the Delete Payload

Configure your API client (Bruno / Postman / similar):

  • Method: POST
  • URL: Service URL from Step 1
  • Auth: Basic Auth — username/password from Step 2
  • Content-Type: text/xml
  • Add a WS-Addressing header: wsa:MessageID with value urn:uuid:<unique-uuid>

 

If you are using Bruno, add this Pre-Request script to auto-generate the UUID:

 

// Bruno Pre-Request Script
const { v4: uuidv4 } = require('uuid');
const messageId = 'urn:uuid:' + uuidv4();
bru.setVar('myMessageId', messageId);

 

Then reference it in the SOAP Header as: {{myMessageId}}

 

Below is a complete example delete payload with fully dummy values. Replace the highlighted fields with values from the original SES create payload (see the field reference table below):

 

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<soapenv:Envelope
    xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
    xmlns:wsa="http://www.w3.org/2005/08/addressing">

  <soapenv:Header>
    <wsa:MessageID>{{myMessageId}}</wsa:MessageID>
  </soapenv:Header>

  <soapenv:Body>
    <n0:ServiceEntrySheetRequestMsg
        xmlns:n0="http://sap.com/xi/SAPGlobal20/Global">

      <MessageHeader>
        <ID>SESTST-20261028-001</ID>
        <ReferenceID>SES-TEST-001</ReferenceID>
        <CreationDateTime>2026-10-01T10:00:00+03:00</CreationDateTime>
        <SenderBusinessSystemID>AN00000000001</SenderBusinessSystemID>
        <RecipientBusinessSystemID>XXXXXXXX</RecipientBusinessSystemID>
        <SenderParty>
          <InternalID>AN00000000002</InternalID>
        </SenderParty>
        <RecipientParty>
          <InternalID>AN00000000001</InternalID>
        </RecipientParty>
        <BusinessScope>
          <TypeCode> </TypeCode>
          <InstanceID schemeID=""> </InstanceID>
        </BusinessScope>
      </MessageHeader>

      <ServiceEntrySheetEntity>
        <ActionCode>03</ActionCode>
        <ApprovalStatus>20</ApprovalStatus>
        <DeleteInApproval>true</DeleteInApproval>
        <ServiceEntrySheet> </ServiceEntrySheet>
        <ServiceEntrySheetName>SES-TEST-001</ServiceEntrySheetName>
        <PurchaseOrder>4500000001</PurchaseOrder>
        <ResponsiblePerson> </ResponsiblePerson>

        <ServiceEntrySheetItemList>
          <ServiceEntrySheetItemEntity>
            <ActionCode>03</ActionCode>
            <ConfirmedQuantity unitCode="E51">1.0</ConfirmedQuantity>
            <NetPriceAmount currencyCode="USD">1000.0</NetPriceAmount>
            <PurchaseOrderItem>10</PurchaseOrderItem>
            <QuanitityUnit>E51</QuanitityUnit>
            <Service>8000000001</Service>
            <ServiceEntrySheetItem>1</ServiceEntrySheetItem>
            <ServiceEntrySheetItemReference>1</ServiceEntrySheetItemReference>
            <ServiceEntrySheetItemDesc>Sample Service Description</ServiceEntrySheetItemDesc>
            <ServicePerformanceDate>2026-10-01T12:00:00+03:00</ServicePerformanceDate>
            <ServicePerformanceEndDate>2026-10-05T12:00:00+03:00</ServicePerformanceEndDate>
            <WorkItem> </WorkItem>
          </ServiceEntrySheetItemEntity>
        </ServiceEntrySheetItemList>

      </ServiceEntrySheetEntity>
    </n0:ServiceEntrySheetRequestMsg>
  </soapenv:Body>
</soapenv:Envelope>

 

Important: Keep all MessageHeader fields (SenderBusinessSystemID, RecipientBusinessSystemID, SenderParty, RecipientParty, CreationDateTime) identical to the original create payload. The <ID> field must be a short unique identifier — max 35 characters. Do NOT put the full urn:uuid string in the <ID> field; the UUID belongs only in the wsa:MessageID SOAP header.

 

Field Reference — Where to Get Each Value

The original create payload can be found in the message monitoring in S/4HANA. Use the values from that payload unchanged - only the ActionCode and DeleteInApproval are different for the delete.

Verifying the Result

After sending the payload, confirm the delete was processed successfully:

 

  1. In S/4HANA: Open the Manage Service Entry Sheets Fiori app its status should show as Deleted.
  2. Check the PO: Open the PO in the Manage Purchase Orders app — the consumed/open quantity on the relevant PO line should be released.
  3. For errors: Monitor Messages (or use the AIF Monitor Fiori app) to check if the inbound message was processed successfully or if there is an error that needs to be resolved.

Related Information

  • Scope Item 42K — Automation of Source-to-Pay with SAP Business Network
  • Communication Arrangement SAP_COM_0237 — Ariba Network Buyer Integration via SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway
  • SAP Component: MM-PUR-GF-ES-2Cl (Service Entry Sheet)

 

Final Thoughts

A stuck Service Entry Sheet that originated from SAP Business Network is a frustrating but solvable problem. The root cause — the missing cancel option for suppliers — is a single configuration setting in Business Network that many buyers have not enabled. Turning it on resolves the issue permanently for all future cases.

 

For cases that are already stuck, the manual SOAP payload approach gives you full control to send the exact delete instruction that S/4HANA expects, using the same interface that SAP Business Network uses internally. The key is to take the values from the original create payload and change only the ActionCode to 03 and set DeleteInApproval to true.

 

Hope this helps someone who has been going in circles trying to figure out why the SES cannot be deleted! If you have questions or a different scenario, drop them in the comments below.

entry.title: Purchase Order Accruals calculation
entry.content:
Dear All,

We onboard a consultant on a six-month contract with a daily rate of GBP 100. As per the contract agreement, the maximum billable days are limited to 22 days per month.

We do not use the Service Entry Sheet (SES) concept in SAP. Therefore, we need to manage the Purchase Order (PO) and monthly accrual postings without service entry confirmations.

We are facing the following challenges:

Scenario 1: Maintaining the PO quantity as 6 months

If we maintain the PO order quantity as six months, the system calculates the PO value based on 180 days × GBP 100, resulting in GBP 18,000. This is incorrect because the contractual maximum is 22 billable days per month.

The system also calculates accruals based on the actual calendar days in each month (30 or 31 days), resulting in incorrect accrual amounts.

Scenario 2: Maintaining the PO quantity as 132 days

If we maintain the PO order quantity as 132 days (22 days × 6 months), the PO value is correctly calculated as GBP 13,200.

However, the accrual calculation is still incorrect. For example, for October 2026, SAP calculates an accrual of GBP 3,100 (31 calendar days × GBP 100) instead of the expected GBP 2,200 (22 billable days × GBP 100).

Clarification Required

How can we achieve the correct PO valuation and monthly accrual calculations using standard SAP functionality, considering that we do not use Service Entry Sheets?

Our requirements are:

Maintain the PO value at GBP 13,200 for the six-month contract.
Calculate monthly accruals based on 22 billable days, resulting in GBP 2,200 per month.
Prevent the system from calculating accruals based on calendar days.
Use standard SAP PO and accrual functionality without custom development, wherever possible.
Please advise on the recommended standard SAP configuration and process to ensure that both the PO value and monthly accrual postings are aligned with the contractual terms, without using the Service Entry Sheet process.

 

Thanks

Naveen

entry.title: Re: Consuming Released API in RAP action handler
entry.content:
Hi Imteyaz,

Short answer: for supplier confirmations there is no released RAP BO you could call with EML, so the released API is the way, and yes, you pay the HTTP round trip. I checked the release states on S/4HANA 2023 and 2025, and both look the same.

What the release information says (table ARS_W_API_STATE, in both releases)

  • The service group API_SUPPLIERCONFIRMATION and the entities A_SupplierConfirmation, A_SupplierConfirmationItem and A_SupplierConfirmationLine are released with contract C2, which is the contract for remote use.
  • No supplier confirmation behavior definition is released with C1, the contract for local use that EML needs in ABAP Cloud. The behavior definition A_SUPPLIERCONFIRMATION exists but has no release state, and neither do the RAP BOs of the apps, R_SupplierConfirmationTP and C_SupplierConfirmationTP.
  • I_PurchaseOrderTP_2 is released C1, but it has no confirmation entity, in 2023 or in 2025. It covers header, item, schedule line, account assignment, pricing element, notes, partner, supplier address, invoicing plan and subcontracting component.
  • For reading there is good news: I_POSupplierConfirmationAPI01 is released C1. Your checks after the Excel upload can read the existing confirmations with a normal SELECT, without HTTP.
  • For the call itself, /IWBEP/CL_CP_FACTORY_REMOTE is released C1, with CREATE_V2_REMOTE_PROXY and CREATE_V4_REMOTE_PROXY. A local client proxy also exists (/IWBEP/CL_CP_CLIENT_PROXY_FACT, CREATE_V4_LOCAL_PROXY), and it would skip HTTP, but it has no release state. So it is not an option for ABAP Cloud.

So, is it a good approach?

When there is no released BO, the released remote API is the way that keeps you on released objects only. The other way out, EML on R_SupplierConfirmationTP from classic ABAP, would work against an object without any contract, and an upgrade can change it without notice. I would not go there for something that posts documents.

What I would do in your case: keep all the validations on the C1 views (I_POSupplierConfirmationAPI01 and the purchase order views), and call the API only for the write, through the remote proxy and a communication arrangement. Then the HTTP part is only the posting, not the reads.

What I did not test: the API call itself through the remote proxy, how long it takes per confirmation, and S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, where the list of released objects can be different. If your system is a newer release, check the release state of R_SupplierConfirmationTP there, because SAP keeps releasing BOs.
